chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Salama b. al-Khattab from 'Ali b. al-Hasan from Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Mu'addab from 'Asim b. Humayd from Khalid al-Qalanisi. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said:

An elderly man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be given his book. On its apparent side — that which faces the people — nothing will be seen but sins. That will be prolonged upon him, so he will say: 'O my Lord! Will You command me to the Fire?' So the Almighty, exalted is His Majesty, will say: 'O elderly man! Indeed, I am ashamed to punish you while you used to pray in the abode of this world. Take My servant to Paradise.'

key_terms.الْجَبَّار: The Almighty (al-Jabbar) — a divine name emphasizing God's irresistible power
key_terms.تُصَلِّي: To pray (salat) — the ritual prayer that saved the elderly man
key_terms.مَسَاوِئ: Misdeeds/sins — the evil acts recorded in one's book of deeds

ai.seo_question: What saves a sinful person on the Day of Judgment according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates a powerful eschatological scene: on the Day of Resurrection, an old man whose record shows only sins will plead with God, and the Almighty will spare him from punishment solely because he used to perform the ritual prayer (salat) in this world. This hadith underscores the supreme importance of prayer as a saving act, and illustrates the boundless divine mercy that can override a lifetime of sin.
